papers.title: Sample Bank — English + हिन्दी
papers.description: A showcase bank: MathML formulas and chemical equations, tables and pictures in the question, the options and the explanation, single and multiple correct answers, English and Hindi, reading passages shared by a group of questions, plus deliberate edge cases.

question_elements.content: Which two statements about the states of matter are correct?

a.content: A gas has a fixed volume but no fixed shape.

b.content: A liquid keeps its volume but takes the shape of its container.

c.content: A solid has both a fixed shape and a fixed volume.

d.content: All three states are compressible to the same degree.

explanation_elements.content: Liquids and solids both have definite volume, and only solids have a definite shape. Gases have neither, and they compress readily, so (a) and (d) are both wrong.

question_elements.content: The diagram shows one molecule of water. How many atoms does it contain?

explanation_elements.content: The picture shows a single molecule made of one oxygen atom and two hydrogen atoms, so three atoms in total. One molecule is the smallest unit that still has the formula
<math><msub><mi>H</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mi>O</mi></math>

question_elements.content: Which of these chemical equations are balanced?

explanation_elements.content: <math><mn>2</mn><msub><mi>H</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo>+</mo><msub><mi>O</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo>→</mo><mn>2</mn><msub><mi>H</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mi>O</mi></math>
balances: four hydrogen atoms and two oxygen atoms on each side.
<math><mi>Na</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>Cl</mi><mo>→</mo><mi>NaCl</mi></math>
balances with one atom of each element on both sides. The other two do not conserve atoms.

question_elements.content: Use the table to answer: which element has the atomic number 17?

explanation_elements.content: Reading across the row that starts with 17 gives the symbol Cl and the name Chlorine. Atomic numbers increase with the number of protons, so 17 protons is chlorine.

question_elements.content: The table lists four acids. Which two are mineral (inorganic) acids rather than organic acids?

explanation_elements.content: Sulfuric and nitric acids contain no carbon and are classed as mineral acids. Acetic and citric acids are organic because they are built on a carbon chain.

question_elements.content: रासायनिक संयोजन में क्या संरक्षित रहता है?
(Which quantity is conserved in a chemical reaction?)

explanation_elements.content: रासायनिक संयोजन में परमाणुओं की संख्या बदलती नहीं है, इसलिए द्रव्यमान और आवेश दोनों संरक्षित रहते हैं।
<math><mn>2</mn><msub><mi>H</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo>+</mo><msub><mi>O</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo>→</mo><mn>2</mn><msub><mi>H</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mi>O</mi></math>
में बाईं और दाईं ओर परमाणुओं की गिनती समान है।

question_elements.content: A car starts from rest and accelerates at a constant rate. Using
<math><mi>v</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>u</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>a</mi><mi>t</mi></math>
, which quantities stay constant?

explanation_elements.content: <math><mi>v</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>u</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>a</mi><mi>t</mi></math>
treats u and a as fixed inputs, so both stay constant, while the velocity grows from zero and the elapsed time keeps increasing. Two worked rows:
Only the last column changes between rows, which is exactly why velocity cannot be the constant.

question_elements.content: What time does the clock show?

explanation_elements.content: The short hour hand points at 3 and the long minute hand points at 12, which is three o'clock.

question_elements.content: The spectrum runs from violet down to red. Which formula links the energy of a single photon to its frequency?

explanation_elements.content: <math><mi>E</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>h</mi><mi>ν</mi></math>
ties a photon's energy to its frequency, where h is Planck's constant.
<math><mi>E</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>m</mi><msup><mi>c</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></math>
is mass-energy equivalence and says nothing about frequency. Red sits at the lowest-frequency end of the spectrum shown, so it carries the least energy per photon.

question_elements.content: The roots of a quadratic equation are given by

<math><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mrow><mo>−</mo><mi>b</mi><mo>±</mo><msqrt><mrow><msup><mi>b</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>−</mo><mn>4</mn><mi>a</mi><mi>c</mi></mrow></msqrt></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn><mi>a</mi></mrow></mfrac></math>
. Which expression is the sum of the two roots?

explanation_elements.content: Adding the two branches cancels the square root and leaves
<math><mo>−</mo><mfrac><mi>b</mi><mi>a</mi></mfrac></math>
, which is the standard sum-of-roots result.

question_elements.content: In the bar chart, which two bars are taller than bar C?

explanation_elements.content: Bar C stands at 45. Bar B reaches 70 and bar D reaches 90, so both clear it, while bar A at 30 does not.

question_elements.content: A car covers 240 km in 4 hours and then 150 km in 2 hours. What is its average speed for the whole journey?

explanation_elements.content: Average speed is total distance over total time, 390 ÷ 6, which is 65 km/h. Taking the mean of the two leg speeds instead gives 67.5 km/h, which is wrong because the faster leg covered less time.

question_elements.content: भारतीय संख्या पद्धति में 47 का अंतिम अंक क्या है?

explanation_elements.content: दशमलव प्रणाली में संख्या 47 के दाहिने सातवाँ अंक इकाई का है, इसलिए अंतिम अंक 7 है।

question_elements.content: A right-angled triangle has the measurements below. What is the length of the hypotenuse?

explanation_elements.content: The diagram shows the right angle at A, which is what makes side BC the hypotenuse:
Pythagoras gives
<math><msup><mi>c</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>=</mo><msup><mi>a</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><msup><mi>b</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></math>
so the hypotenuse is √(25 + 144) = √169 = 13 cm.

question_elements.content: Differentiate
<math><mi>f</mi><mo>(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>)</mo><mo>=</mo><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>3</mn></msup><mo>−</mo><mn>6</mn><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mn>9</mn><mi>x</mi></math>
and find every value of
<math><msup><mi>f</mi><mo>′</mo></msup><mo>(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>)</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>3</mn><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>−</mo><mn>12</mn><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>9</mn></math>
that equals zero.

explanation_elements.content: Differentiating term by term gives
<math><msup><mi>f</mi><mo>′</mo></msup><mo>(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>)</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>3</mn><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>−</mo><mn>12</mn><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>9</mn></math>
, which factors as
<math><mn>3</mn><mo>(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>)</mo><mo>(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>3</mn><mo>)</mo></math>
. It vanishes at x = 1 and x = 3, and the table agrees: f(1) = 4 and f(3) = 0 are the turning points.

question_elements.content: In how many ways can five people be seated in a row if two of them insist on sitting together?

explanation_elements.content: Treat the pair as one block: the block plus the other three people is 4 units, giving
<math><mn>4</mn><mo>!</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>24</mn></math>
arrangements, and the two inside the block can swap, giving
<math><mn>24</mn><mo>×</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>48</mn></math>
. Ignoring the constraint would give 5! = 120, which is option (d).

question_elements.content: Find the sum of the first 20 terms of
<math><mn>3</mn><mo>+</mo><mn>7</mn><mo>+</mo><mn>11</mn><mo>+</mo><mo>⋯</mo></math>
using

<math><msub><mi>S</mi><mi>n</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mi>n</mi><mn>2</mn></mfrac><mo>(</mo><mn>2</mn><mi>a</mi><mo>+</mo><mo>(</mo><mi>n</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>)</mo><mi>d</mi><mo>)</mo></math>

explanation_elements.content: Here a = 3 and d = 4, so the twentieth term is 3 + 19 × 4 = 79 and the sum is
<math><mfrac><mi>n</mi><mn>2</mn></mfrac><mo>(</mo><mn>2</mn><mi>a</mi><mo>+</mo><mo>(</mo><mi>n</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>)</mo><mi>d</mi><mo>)</mo></math>
<math><mn>820</mn></math>

question_elements.content: A fair six-sided die is rolled twice. What is the probability that the two numbers add up to 7?

explanation_elements.content: There are 36 equally likely ordered outcomes and the table lists the 6 that sum to 7, so
<math><mi>P</mi><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mi>w</mi><mn>36</mn></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mn>6</mn><mn>36</mn></mfrac></math>
. Treating the sum as unordered would halve the count and give the wrong 1/12.

question_elements.content: Which two of the four shapes are quadrilaterals? Look at each option and tick every shape with exactly four straight sides.

explanation_elements.content: A quadrilateral is any closed shape with four straight sides. The rectangle and the square both qualify, the triangle has three sides and the pentagon has five.

question_elements.content: The circle shows four sectors labelled A to D. Which two sectors are equal in area?

explanation_elements.content: The sectors run 35, 25, 25 and 15 per cent of the circle. B and C are both 25 per cent, so they are exactly equal in area, while A is the largest and D the smallest.

question_elements.content: Which number is marked on the number line?

explanation_elements.content: The marker sits exactly halfway between 3 and 4, so it reads 3.5. It is well to the left of 7, so 7.5 is not a candidate.

question_elements.content: This question shares the Reading Passages category but belongs to no passage. In the app, what does belonging to a passage change for a question?

a.content: A shared context is shown above it, and tests keep the group together

c.content: Its own bookmark and schedule are replaced by the passage's

d.content: Nothing at all — a passage is decoration

explanation_elements.content: Membership adds the shared context and the group behaviour and nothing else: scheduling, bookmarks, attempts and stats stay per question, which is exactly what this category demonstrates by mixing one standalone question with two passage groups.

question_elements.content: According to the passage, what keeps the water cycle running?

explanation_elements.content: The passage opens with the Sun heating water in oceans and rivers; that energy input drives every later step of the cycle.

question_elements.content: Using the passage's table, which two steps of the cycle take place up in the sky?

explanation_elements.content: Condensation builds clouds and precipitation drops their water, so both happen aloft. Evaporation starts at the surface and collection ends there, which is why the other pairings are wrong.

question_elements.content: In the passage's table, dew on morning grass is listed as an everyday example of which step?

explanation_elements.content: The table's Condensation row names dew on morning grass: water vapour cooling into droplets where the ground is cold. Rain, a drying puddle and a river reaching the sea belong to the other three rows.

question_elements.content: गद्यांश के अनुसार इस शृंखला में उत्पादक कौन है?
(According to the passage, who is the producer in this chain?)

explanation_elements.content: गद्यांश कहता है कि हरे पौधे सूर्य के प्रकाश से अपना भोजन स्वयं बनाते हैं, इसीलिए शृंखला के आरंभ में वे ही उत्पादक हैं। शेष तीनों पौधों पर या एक-दूसरे पर निर्भर रहते हैं।

question_elements.content: ऊर्जा इस शृंखला में कहाँ से प्रवेश करती है?
(Where does the energy enter this chain from?)

explanation_elements.content: पौधे सूर्य के प्रकाश को भोजन में बदलते हैं, इसलिए ऊर्जा शृंखला में सूर्य से ही प्रवेश करती है और फिर क्रम से जीवों तक पहुँचती है।

question_elements.content: Match each ruler to the year their reign in India began. Which two matches are correct?

explanation_elements.content: Akbar acceded in 1556 after Humayun's death, and Babur founded the empire at Panipat in 1526, so (a) and (c) are right.
Aurangzeb took the throne in 1658 and died in 1707, so (b) gives his death, not his accession. Humayun ruled from 1540 and was restored in 1555, never in 1600, so (d) is wrong too.

question_elements.content: भारत में अंग्रेज़ों का स्थापत्य काल कौन-सा था?
(Which period saw British ascendancy in India?)

explanation_elements.content: 1858 में भारत पर क्राउन नियंत्रण स्थापित हुआ और यह 1947 तक रहा। 1757 से 1857 का समय केवल कंपनी शासन का था।

question_elements.content: Which ship carried the Titanic on its maiden voyage, and in which year did it sink?

explanation_elements.content: RMS Titanic struck an iceberg on 15 April 1912 on her maiden voyage. Britannic sank in 1916 during the First World War, and Olympic never sank at all.

question_elements.content: The table lists four dams. Which two stand on the same river?

explanation_elements.content: Read the River column: Bhakra and Nathpa-Jakhal are both on the Sutlej near Bilaspur, the barrage sitting just downstream of the dam. Hirakud is on the Mahanadi and Nagarjuna Sagar on the Krishna, so no other pair matches.

question_elements.content: भारत की सबसे लंबी नदी कौन-सी है?
(Which is the longest river in India?)

explanation_elements.content: गंगा की लंबाई लगभग 2525 किलोमीटर है, जो भारत की किसी भी अन्य नदी से अधिक है, इसलिए यही सही उत्तर है।

question_elements.content: How many players from one team are on the field in a standard association football match?

explanation_elements.content: Each side fields eleven players, one of whom is the goalkeeper, with no substitutes counted until the match is under way.

question_elements.content: Which resting heart rate would most likely belong to a trained endurance athlete?

explanation_elements.content: A larger stroke volume from endurance training lowers resting heart rate, so the lowest resting rate in the table belongs to the trained athlete.

question_elements.content: Select every prime number.

explanation_elements.content: A prime has exactly two positive factors. 2 and 13 qualify; 9 = 3², 21 = 3 × 7 and 1 has a single factor.

question_elements.content: Which three are physical quantities, rather than units?

explanation_elements.content: Length, force and time are quantities; metre and kilogram are the SI units used to measure other quantities.

question_elements.content: A body is thrown straight up. Which statements are true while it is in the air, ignoring air resistance?

a.content: The acceleration is constant and downward.

b.content: The speed decreases all the way to the ground.

c.content: The velocity reverses direction at the top.

d.content: The acceleration is zero at the top.

explanation_elements.content: <math><mi>a</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>g</mi><mo>≈</mo><mn>9.8</mn><mfrac><mi>m</mi><msup><mi>s</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></mfrac></math>
The acceleration stays constant and downward throughout, so it is certainly not zero at the top, and the speed falls to zero then rises again. Only (a) and (c) hold.

question_elements.content: In Newton’s second law the acceleration is proportional to the net external force and inversely proportional to the total mass. Which statement about acceleration follows?

a.content: It <mark>increases</mark> when the net force increases.

b.content: It is independent of the net force.

c.content: It <del>decreases</del> when the net force increases.

d.content: It depends only on the mass, not on the force.

explanation_elements.content: Writing the law as F = ma makes it plain: the acceleration is directly proportional to F and inversely proportional to m, so a bigger force means a bigger acceleration, and a bigger mass means a smaller one. That rules out (b) and (d), and (c) states the opposite of the direct relationship. Since force is measured in newtons (kg·m·s−2) and acceleration in metres per second squared (m·s−2), the mass that appears in each must cancel.

question_elements.content: At constant temperature, Boyle’s law gives
P<sub>1</sub>V<sub>1</sub> = P<sub>2</sub>V<sub>2</sub>. If the absolute pressure on a fixed amount of gas is doubled, what happens to its volume?

explanation_elements.content: P<sub>1</sub>V<sub>1</sub> is constant, so P and V trade places inversely: doubling the pressure halves the volume. The mass of the gas is fixed throughout, which is what rules out (d).

question_elements.content: The SI unit of electric current is the joule ampere. The ampere is itself derived from two other base units. Which two?

explanation_elements.content: One ampere is one coulomb per second, so it is derived from charge and time — the joule struck through in the question is a unit of energy and has no place in an electrical current. None of the other pairs mixes a quantity of charge with a quantity of time.

question_elements.content: What is the capital of Japan? / जापान की राजधानी क्या है?
Choose one option only — the two languages describe the same question.

explanation_elements.content: Tokyo has been the seat of government since 1868, when the capital was moved from Kyoto.

question_elements.content: The table gives the composition of the human body by mass. Which two entries are largest?
मानव शरीर का द्रव्यमान-अनुसार संघटन नीचे दिया गया है।

a.content: Water and Protein / जल और प्रोटीन

b.content: Protein and Fat / प्रोटीन और वसा

c.content: Fat and Mineral salts / वसा और खनिज लवण

d.content: Mineral salts and Carbohydrate / खनिज लवण और कार्बोहाइड्रेट

explanation_elements.content: Water at 60 per cent is the largest single component and protein at 16 per cent is next, so the pair is (a). वही क्रम तालिका से सीधे पढ़ा जा सकता है।

question_elements.content: भारत का संविधान कब लागू हुआ? / When did the Constitution of India come into force?
26 January 1950 is the date to compare against.

explanation_elements.content: The Constitution was adopted on 26 November 1949 but came into force on 26 January 1950, when India became a republic.

question_elements.content: These steps are listed out of order. Which option gives the correct sequence for preparing a sample slide?

explanation_elements.content: Fix first, then cut thin sections, mount those on a slide and stain last, giving 1, 2, 4, 3.

question_elements.content: Rank these states of matter from lowest to highest particle attraction.

explanation_elements.content: Attraction is weakest in a gas, intermediate in a liquid and strongest in a solid, which is why solids keep a fixed shape.

question_elements.content: Rank these planets by their average distance from the Sun, nearest first.

explanation_elements.content: <math><msup><mi>T</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>∝</mo><msup><mi>a</mi><mn>3</mn></msup></math>
tells us that a planet's orbital period grows with its distance from the Sun, and the mean distances rise in the same order: Mercury 57.9, Venus 108.2, Earth 149.6 and Mars 227.9 million kilometres.

question_elements.content: Which three practices make a numerical answer trustworthy?

explanation_elements.content: Units, significant figures and stated assumptions all have to be in place before the number means anything. Guessing sets no basis at all, and rounding early discards precision.

elements.content: The Sun heats water in oceans and rivers. The warm surface turns to vapour and rises; high above, the vapour cools and condenses into droplets that gather as clouds. When the droplets grow heavy they fall back as rain or snow, and the collected water finds its way to the sea. Nothing leaves the system — the same water has circulated for billions of years.

elements.content: Read the passage and the table before answering; the three questions that share this passage all draw on them, and in a test they arrive together with the passage shown above each one.

हरे पौधे सूर्य के प्रकाश से अपना भोजन स्वयं बनाते हैं, इसलिए उन्हें इस शृंखला का उत्पादक कहा जाता है। जो जीव पौधों को खाते हैं वे शाकाहारी कहलाते हैं, और जो शाकाहारियों को खाते हैं वे मांसाहारी। इस प्रकार ऊर्जा सूर्य से पौधों तक और फिर जीवों तक क्रम से पहुँचती है। मृत जीवों को खाने वाले सूक्ष्म जीव मिट्टी को पोषित करते हैं, जिससे यह चक्र फिर आरंभ होता है।
